description: Long-passage calibration for the pre-MoE activation Gram dump. The hook captures PREFILL tokens, so long prompts = more samples. Diverse domains exercise varied expert routing.

prompts.text: The transformer architecture, introduced in 2017, replaced recurrence with self-attention as the primary mechanism for modeling sequences. In a standard encoder block, each token is first projected into query, key, and value vectors. The attention scores are computed as the scaled dot product of queries and keys, normalized with a softmax, and used to form a weighted sum of the value vectors. Multiple attention heads run in parallel, each learning to attend to different relationships, and their outputs are concatenated and projected. Because attention has no inherent notion of order, positional encodings, either sinusoidal or learned, are added to the token embeddings. Each attention sublayer is followed by a position-wise feed-forward network, typically two linear layers with a nonlinearity between them, and both sublayers are wrapped with residual connections and layer normalization. Mixture-of-experts variants replace the dense feed-forward network with a set of expert networks and a router that selects a small subset of experts per token, increasing capacity without a proportional increase in computation. Explain, in detail, how gradients flow back through the attention and feed-forward sublayers during training, and why layer normalization placement, pre-norm versus post-norm, affects training stability in very deep transformer stacks.

The lighthouse had stood on the headland for nearly a century, its white tower streaked with salt and the slow green of lichen. Every evening the keeper climbed the spiral stair, trimmed the wick, and watched the beam sweep out across water that turned from grey to black as the light failed. He kept a journal of the ships he saw, the weather, and the long silences between. One winter, during a storm that bent the gulls sideways and tore shingles from the cottage roof, he found a bottle wedged among the rocks at the base of the tower. Inside was a single sheet of paper, folded many times, the ink blurred but still legible. The message was addressed to no one in particular, and it described a small harbor town on the far side of the sea, a bakery that opened before dawn, and a person waiting who had long since stopped expecting an answer. Continue this story, developing the keeper's decision about what to do with the message, and bring in a second character whose arrival changes the course of the narrative.

When designing a concurrent data structure, the choice between lock-based and lock-free approaches involves trade-offs in throughput, latency, and complexity. A lock-free queue, for example, typically relies on atomic compare-and-swap operations to update head and tail pointers without ever holding a mutex, which avoids priority inversion and deadlock but introduces the ABA problem, where a pointer is changed from A to B and back to A between a thread's read and its compare-and-swap, causing the operation to succeed incorrectly. Solutions include tagged pointers that pack a version counter alongside the address, hazard pointers that prevent reclamation of nodes still referenced by other threads, and epoch-based reclamation that defers freeing memory until all threads have passed a quiescent point. Describe how you would implement a bounded multi-producer multi-consumer ring buffer using atomic operations, explain the memory-ordering constraints required on each load and store to ensure correctness on a weakly ordered architecture, and analyze the failure modes that arise if the acquire and release semantics are weakened.

The Industrial Revolution transformed Britain between roughly 1760 and 1840, shifting production from hand tools in homes and small workshops to powered machinery in factories. The mechanization of textile spinning and weaving, the adoption of the steam engine, and the expansion of coal mining and iron production reshaped the economy and the landscape. Cities such as Manchester and Birmingham grew rapidly as rural workers migrated in search of wage labor, producing crowded housing, polluted air, and new patterns of work governed by the factory clock rather than the seasons. The period also produced profound social consequences: the rise of an industrial working class, debates over child labor and factory conditions, the growth of trade unions, and eventually reform legislation. Analyze the relationship between technological change, capital accumulation, and labor organization during this period, and assess the extent to which rising aggregate output translated into improved living standards for ordinary workers in the first several decades.

Consider the problem of estimating the parameters of a probability distribution from observed data using maximum likelihood. Given a set of independent and identically distributed samples, the likelihood is the product of the density evaluated at each sample, and because products of small numbers underflow, one maximizes the log-likelihood instead, which turns the product into a sum. For many distributions the maximum can be found analytically by setting the gradient of the log-likelihood to zero and solving, but for others, such as mixtures, no closed form exists and iterative methods are required. The expectation-maximization algorithm alternates between computing the expected value of the latent variables given the current parameters and maximizing the resulting expected complete-data log-likelihood, and it is guaranteed to increase the observed-data likelihood at each step though it may converge to a local optimum. Derive the update equations for fitting a mixture of two Gaussians in one dimension, explain why the algorithm cannot decrease the likelihood, and discuss how initialization and the number of components affect the solution.
